newsitem.title: UK: Standard mulls selling Mocatta - paper.
newsitem.headline: Standard mulls selling Mocatta - paper.

text.p: Standard Chartered is considering divesting its Mocatta gold bullion and base metals trading arm, which is not considered part of the bank's core business, the Sunday Telegraph reported.
No one at Standard Chartered was available to comment.
The Sunday Telegraph cited an unnamed observer as saying, "If you are asking me whether it will be part of the group in a year's time, the answer is probably not."
The paper said the sale or float of Mocatta -- founded in 1671 and one of the world's largest bullion dealers -- might raise up to 200 million stg.
The bank paved the way for the Mocatta disposal earlier this month when the management of the gold and base metals business were merged under one head, the Sunday Telegraph said.
It added that Standard Chartered believed Moccata was not core to its main retail and corporate banking business.
The bank sold its private banking business to Swiss Bank Corp earlier this year.
